title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a transitional page in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes, the sequel to La Longue Marche. On the previous page Grothendieck checked that three involutions τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞ satisfy the relations (23): τ'^2 = 1, (τ'_0τ'_∞)^2 = 1, (τ'_1τ'_0)^3 = 1. These are the defining relations of the (2,3,∞) hyperbolic reflection (Coxeter) group, i.e. the extended modular group PGL(2,Z). The orientation-preserving products l' satisfy l'_∞ l'_1 l'_0 = 1, l'_1^2 = 1, l'_∞^3 = 1. That is the presentation PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3.

Here he announces he wants to make explicit the relation between the group \tilde{Π'_{0,3}} ≅ 𝔖_{0,3} and GP(1,Z) ≅ Gl(2,Z)' := Gl(2,Z)/{±1} = PGL(2,Z). 𝔖_{0,3} is a symmetry or 'extended' group attached to the 3-punctured sphere, built with orientation-reversing elements. It is identified with a group Aut_ext(Π_{0,3}) of 'non-oriented' (anti-)geographic automorphisms. Here Π_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, free of rank 2.

To set this up he recalls (26) PGL(2,R) ≅ GL(2,R)/R^* ≅ GL(2,R)^{±1}/{±1}, where GL(2,R)^{±1} means the matrices of determinant ±1. This holds because scaling by λ multiplies det by λ², so every matrix can be normalised to det ±1, uniquely up to sign. PGL(2,R) acts on the Poincaré half-plane D = {Im z > 0} (27) by (28): z ↦ (az+b)/(cz+d) if det > 0, and z ↦ (a z̄+b)/(c z̄+d) if det < 0. He states that this identifies PGL(2,R) with the group of conformal and anti-conformal automorphisms of D, i.e. the full isometry group of the hyperbolic plane. A margin note observes that PGL(2,R) is disconnected, with identity component PSL(2,R) ≅ GL(2,R)^+/R^{*+}.

He then begins the standard modular dictionary.
- A complex elliptic curve E is the same as a pair (V, π): a 1-dimensional C-vector space V and a lattice π ⊂ V, i.e. a discrete subgroup of rank 2. The margin calls this an obvious equivalence of categories.
- The complex orientation of V picks a generator of ∧²_Z π, so π is canonically oriented.
- On the next page, a 'rigidification' (an oriented basis e_1, e_2 with e_1 ∧ e_2 = η) normalises e_1 = 1 and e_2 = τ ∈ D.
- This yields the action of SL(2,Z) on D by Möbius transformations, i.e. the orbifold M_{1,1} = SL(2,Z)\\D.

The purpose is to interpret the combinatorially defined group of the 3-punctured sphere as PGL(2,Z) acting on D. This links the M_{0,3}/P^1−{0,1,∞} picture to the M_{1,1} picture (elliptic curves, the Legendre/λ-covering), a theme of the Long March and of the Teichmüller tower in the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical errors. Formula (28) is correct: for det u < 0 one has Im f_u(z) = −det(u)·Im z̄ / |c z̄ + d|^2 > 0, and z ↦ conjugation commutes with real Möbius maps, so u ↦ f_u is a homomorphism. The isomorphisms in (26) are correct.
'automorphismes conformes' must be read as conformal OR anti-conformal; otherwise only PSL(2,R) would be obtained. The determinant convention in (28) makes this clear.

The definition Aut_ext(Π_{0,3}) := Gl(2,Z)/{±1} is a definition by fiat on this page. Its intended meaning (outer automorphisms preserving the three cusp classes up to the extended symmetry) is not justified here. Note that Out(F_2) itself is GL(2,Z), not PGL(2,Z), so the 'ext' structure must be extra data.

ideas.what: PGL(2,R) ≅ GL(2,R)^{±1}/{±1} acting on the upper half-plane, with det<0 elements acting via z̄; identification with the full group of conformal/anticonformal automorphisms (hyperbolic isometries)

ideas.what: Complex elliptic curves ⇔ (1-dim C-vector space, lattice); canonical orientation of the lattice via ∧²π; rigidified curves ⇔ τ ∈ D
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization of elliptic curves; moduli M_{1,1} = SL(2,Z)\\H with framings
ideas.where_published: Classical; Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Identifying the extended symmetry group of the 3-punctured sphere (generated by involutions τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞ with Coxeter relations (2,3,∞)) with PGL(2,Z) = GL(2,Z)/±1
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,∞) reflection triangle group; Out of free group and the Γ_{0,3}/Γ_{1,1} link

ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche (1981); the Esquisse mentions the (2,3,∞) and SL(2,Z) relationship to dessins

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an expository recollection of standard facts: the PGL(2,R) action on the half-plane including anticonformal maps, and the lattice description of elliptic curves. It sets up the known identification of the 3-punctured-sphere symmetry group with PGL(2,Z). There is nothing new; the only interest is seeing Grothendieck's notation (GP(1,Z), Gl(2,Z)', 𝔖_{0,3}) and the intended bridge between M_{0,3} and M_{1,1}.
transcription_corrections: Margin note at left (diagonal) reads roughly: 'NB GP(1,R) n'est pas connexe, i.e. [composante neutre ?] ... Gl(2,R)^+ ... Sl(2,R)/±1 ... Gl(2,R)^{±1} [?]'. The transcription's 'contient strictement[?]' is doubtful.
Margin note under 'Π̃'_{0,3} ≃ 𝔖_{0,3}' appears to read 'quasi-[anti-?]géographiques non orientés' (an annotation qualifying the automorphisms), consistent with the transcription but uncertain.
Margin note near the elliptic-curve sentence: 'équivalence de catégories évid.', with the word 'réseau' in quotes: correct.
'sous-groupe discret de rg 2' is correct; it is not 'vg 2'.
